monthly_review.summary: September has started with dramatically lower volume and markedly higher physiological strain compared to August — a sharp decline in workload paired with signs of residual fatigue.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 45 km less and 8 fewer sessions, average heart rate rose by 10 bpm while pace improved — strongly indicating reduced parasympathetic tone and compensatory effort, not fitness gain.

goal_tracker.message: Catching up to last month’s 51.3 km would require ~1.6 km/day for 28 days — but readiness is compromised, so chasing that number risks further fatigue accumulation or injury; volume should remain low and purposeful until recovery metrics rebound.

insights.title: Elevated HR at low intensities signals sympathetic dominance
insights.body: Avg HR increased +10 bpm from Aug to Sep while avg pace improved by 62 sec/km — and recent easy runs (e.g., 2026-09-01: 9:36 min/km @ 140 bpm; 2026-08-23: 10:51 min/km @ 111 bpm) confirm disproportionate cardiac output for sub-threshold efforts.

insights.title: Worsening efficiency correlates with aerobic TE decline
insights.body: Avg efficiency rose from 14.12 (Aug) to 15.42 (Sep) — a +1.30 ml/kg/km deterioration — while avg aerobic TE fell from 2.6 to 2.3, suggesting reduced metabolic stability during steady-state efforts.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length variability indicate fatigue adaptation
insights.body: Cadence dropped sharply in two recent runs (138–139 spm on 2026-09-01 and 2026-08-23) versus typical 148–159 spm, while stride length swung from 65.7 cm (2026-08-23) to 101.8 cm (2026-09-03) — a 55% range — likely reflecting inconsistent neuromuscular control under fatigue.

insights.title: Ground contact time spikes align with low-effort runs
insights.body: Two of the three longest ground contact times (385 ms on 2026-08-23, 389 ms on 2026-09-01) occurred during very slow, low-HR runs — a known marker of reduced neuromuscular readiness and delayed elastic recoil.

recommendations.action: Complete one 30-min Zone 1 walk or very light jog (HR ≤120 bpm, pace ≥12:00 min/km) on Tuesday — no distance target, only rhythm and breath awareness.
recommendations.reason: To stimulate vagal tone without cardiovascular load; matches compromised readiness status and counters elevated baseline HR.

recommendations.action: Perform 10 minutes of guided diaphragmatic breathing (5-sec inhale, 6-sec exhale) each evening before bed, tracked via HRV app if available.
recommendations.reason: Directly targets autonomic imbalance evidenced by high HR at low intensities and absent recovery metrics.
